description.p: BookiE is a fast, native database client for Linux. It connects to PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, and ClickHouse, with experimental Redis and MongoDB support. It lets you browse tables, edit data in place, run SQL, and tunnel through SSH bastions, all from a clean GTK4 / libadwaita interface.

ul.li: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, and ClickHouse drivers
PostgreSQL TCP, TLS, SSH, and local Unix-socket connections
In-place cell editing with primary-key safety
SQL editor with syntax highlighting and Run / Cancel
SSH tunneling with TOFU host-key checking
TLS, read-only mode, auto-reconnect, and saved connections
Multi-tab workspace with structure / DDL editor

description.p: Preserve exact values across the database drivers and exports: zero dates, negative and extended MySQL times, SQL Server time zone offsets, ClickHouse decimal scale and fractional seconds, PostgreSQL arrays and eras, and exact decimal parameters. CSV keeps empty text distinct from NULL.

Preserve SQL literal syntax when formatting, prevent boolean affinity mismatches from entering edits, validate PostgreSQL decoder boundaries, and execute isolated widget and keyring regressions in CI.
BookiE 0.1.3: new app icon, and rust_decimal no longer pulls the unused rkyv 0.7 advisory.
BookiE 0.1.2: binary values in a TEXT column stay display-only, so a commit cannot overwrite the blob with a byte-count label.

BookiE 0.1.1: Jump to Column, complete SQL drafts, dialect-safe formatting, and PostgreSQL values that no longer appear as false NULLs. Server Activity still shows session duration. Legacy tablepro commands remain available.
